title: Federalism

questions.q: What is the structure of a federation?
questions.answer: A federation is usually formed at two levels: the central government and the regions (states, provinces, territories).

questions.q: Why is Brazil an exception in federalism?
questions.answer: Brazil is an exception because the 1988 Constitution included the municipalities as autonomous political entities, making the federation tripartite, encompassing the Union, the States, and the municipalities.

questions.q: What is the 1988 Constitution of Brazil?
questions.answer: The 1988 Constitution of Brazil included the municipalities as autonomous political entities, making the federation tripartite.

questions.q: What is the relationship between states and municipalities in Brazil?
questions.answer: Each state is divided into municipalities (municípios) with their own legislative council (câmara de vereadores) and a mayor (prefeito), which are partly autonomous from both Federal and State Government.

questions.q: What is the organic law of a municipality in Brazil?
questions.answer: Each municipality has a 'little constitution', called 'organic law' (lei orgânica).

questions.q: What is the status of municipalities in Mexico?
questions.answer: In Mexico, municipalities are granted full-autonomy by the federal constitution and their existence as autonomous entities (municipio libre, 'free municipality') is established by the federal government and cannot be revoked by the states' constitutions.

questions.q: What powers and competencies belong exclusively to municipalities in Mexico?
questions.answer: The federal constitution determines which powers and competencies belong exclusively to the municipalities and not to the constituent states.

questions.q: Do municipalities in Mexico have an elected legislative assembly?
questions.answer: No, municipalities do not have an elected legislative assembly.

questions.q: What channels did Perotti examine in his 1996 study on how inequality affects economic growth?
questions.answer: Perotti examined the channels through which inequality may affect economic growth, including human capital formation, fertility, redistributive taxation, private savings, investment, and political and social stability.

triples.o: the channels through which inequality may affect economic growth

questions.q: What did Perotti find about the relationship between inequality and human capital formation?

triples.o: lower level of human capital formation

questions.q: What did Perotti find about the relationship between inequality and fertility?
questions.answer: Perotti showed that inequality is associated with higher level of fertility.

questions.q: What did Perotti find about the relationship between inequality and redistributive taxation?
questions.answer: Perotti found that inequality is associated with higher levels of redistributive taxation, which is associated with lower levels of growth from reductions in private savings and investment.

triples.o: lower levels of growth from reductions in private savings and investment

questions.q: What did Perotti conclude about more equal societies?

questions.q: What is the Mariana Trench?
questions.answer: The Mariana Trench is the deepest part of the world's oceans.

questions.q: Where is the Mariana Trench located?
questions.answer: The Mariana Trench is located in the western Pacific Ocean, an average of 200 kilometres to the east of the Mariana Islands, in the Western Pacific East of Philippines.

questions.q: What is the length of the Mariana Trench?
questions.answer: The Mariana Trench measures about 2,550 km (1,580 mi) long.

questions.q: What is the width of the Mariana Trench?
questions.answer: The Mariana Trench is 69 km (43 mi) wide on average.

questions.q: What is the maximum depth of the Mariana Trench?
questions.answer: The Mariana Trench reaches a maximum-known depth of 10,994 metres (36,070 ft) at the Challenger Deep, although some unrepeated measurements place the deepest portion at 11,034 metres (36,201 ft).

questions.q: What is the Challenger Deep?
questions.answer: The Challenger Deep is a small slot-shaped valley in the floor of the Mariana Trench, at its southern end, where the trench reaches its maximum-known depth.

questions.q: When was the Mariana Trench established as a United States National Monument?

title: Blue whale

questions.q: What does the blue whale eat?
questions.answer: The blue whale eats krill, and also incidentally consumes small fish, crustaceans and squid.

questions.q: How much krill can an adult blue whale eat in a day?
questions.answer: An adult blue whale can eat up to 40 million krill in a day, sometimes eating up to 3,600 kilograms (7,900 lb) of krill in a single day.

triples.o: up to 40 million krill in a day
up to 3,600 kilograms (7,900 lb) of krill in a single day

questions.q: What is the daily energy requirement of an adult blue whale?
questions.answer: The daily energy requirement of an adult blue whale is in the region of 1.5 million kilocalories (6.3 GJ).

questions.q: At what depths do blue whales typically feed?
questions.answer: Blue whales typically feed at depths of more than 100 metres (330 ft) during the day and only surface-feed at night.

triples.o: more than 100 metres (330 ft) during the day

questions.q: How long can blue whales dive when feeding?
questions.answer: Dive times are typically 10 minutes when feeding, though dives of up to 21 minutes are possible.

questions.q: How does the blue whale feed?
questions.answer: The blue whale feeds by lunging forward at groups of krill, taking the animals and a large quantity of water into its mouth; the water is then squeezed out through the baleen plates by pressure from the ventral pouch and tongue, and the remaining krill are swallowed.

questions.answer: It flows near the surface, then at the Rheinbrech falls into the depths, reappears at the northern German shore off Lindau, follows the northern shore to Hagnau am Bodensee, with a small fraction diverted off Mainau into Lake Überlingen, and most flows via the Constance hopper into the Rheinrinne and Seerhein.

questions.q: What is the Rheinbrech?
questions.answer: The Rheinbrech is the point where the Rhine water abruptly falls into the depths of Lake Constance because of the greater density of cold water.

questions.q: What is the Rheinrinne?
questions.answer: The Rheinrinne, also called the Rhine Gutter, is a channel in Lake Constance through which most of the Rhine water flows.

questions.q: What is the Seerhein?
questions.answer: The Seerhein is a waterway that most of the Rhine water flows into via the Constance hopper and Rheinrinne.

questions.q: Where is Lindau located?
questions.answer: Lindau is an island in Lake Constance, off the northern German shore.

questions.q: Where is Mainau located?
questions.answer: Mainau is an island in Lake Constance where a small fraction of the Rhine flow is diverted into Lake Überlingen.
